text:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — we just received a DSAR delete for user id=U-9982. During a maintenance window a transient role (transient_read) was granted to svc-archive and there are snapshots that may contain embeddings. Need quick guidance: how to prove erase propagation + what audit/KMS artifacts we must produce for legal. cc @Emily R @Samir Khan

Jordan Patel: Which region/tenant and snapshot path? Also did the keystore rotate recently? If the key rotated after delete we may not be able to decrypt to confirm contents.

Maria Chen: Tenant eu-west-1 / acct 9982. Snapshot path: s3://redwood-backups/prod/9982/2026-03-18-01.snap. KMS alias: alias/rdw-prod-eu. Keystore rotation happened yesterday at 03:12 UTC (keystore:v3 -> v4).

Samir Khan: Ok — two immediate flags: 1) ephemeral role grant needs an audit record showing grant + revoke (who/when). 2) KMS rotation after the delete can complicate content verification. For DSAR we typically provide a signed erasure receipt: signed audit bundle + list of pruned snapshot IDs + KMS key version metadata. We should check CloudTrail/AuditLog for IAM:GrantRole and IAM:RevokeRole and look for kms:GenerateDataKey/kms:Decrypt calls from svc-archive around the window.

infra-bot: deploy-log: role-grant event recorded: grant_id=gr-34211 actor=ops-rotation@infra svc=iam target=svc-archive role=transient_read ts=2026-03-18T02:08:22Z

Maria Chen: here's the minimal log snippet I pulled:```
2026-03-18T02:08:22Z INFO grant_role actor=ops-rotation@infra target=svc-archive role=transient_read grant_id=gr-34211
2026-03-18T02:09:05Z INFO revoke_role actor=ops-rotation@infra target=svc-archive role=transient_read grant_id=gr-34211
2026-03-18T02:10:30Z INFO snapshot_access actor=svc-archive action=read snapshot=s3://redwood-backups/prod/9982/2026-03-18-01.snap
```

Samir Khan: That helps. Next: we need evidence of snapshot prune/delete events and any S3 lifecycle or manual delete operations. If the snapshot was deleted after rotation, include the S3 delete markers and the kms:DisableKey or ReEncryptMetadata events if any. Also generate an audit bundle and have the platform KMS Sign the bundle so legal can verify chain-of-custody. Use `tools/erasure_proof --tenant 9982 --snap 2026-03-18-01` to produce the initial proof.

Jordan Patel: Note: if the keystore rotated (v3 -> v4) and old key material is not available, we can't decrypt the snapshot to show plaintext deletion. Legal ok with signed metadata + access logs and delete markers? @Emily R can confirm.

Emily R: For DSAR we accept cryptographically-signed audit bundles + S3 deletion markers + KMS key version metadata as proof in most cases. If decrypting content to demonstrate redaction is required, we will need a retention exception and an explicit justification. In short: signed audit bundle + kms key ids + snapshot delete evidence should satisfy the requester for a standard erase. If there is any retention hold, escalate.

Samir Khan: Action plan: 1) Freeze writes for uid U-9982 (Maria), 2) infra to snapshot current state and capture S3 delete markers / lifecycle rules (Jordan), 3) security to produce signed audit bundle (me) via KMS Sign and attach grant/revoke + snapshot_access logs, 4) legal to confirm bundle format suffices (Emily). Target: initial packet in 8 hours.

Maria Chen: Acknowledged. I'll block writes and add a retention hold flag to the DSAR until we have the signed proof. Assigning tasks in the ticket. Thanks all :thumbsup:

privacy-bot: DSAR tracker updated: request=DSAR-2026-114, status=collecting-proof, owner=Maria Chen

Samir Khan: I'll kick off the `erasure_proof` run and post the signed bundle here when ready. If we hit decryption gaps due to rotation, we'll note that explicitly on the receipt and include key rotation timestamps.

Maria Chen: Perfect — please include which KMS key versions were used to sign and any internal ticket IDs. Closing loop once the signed bundle is attached. :sparkles:
